$comment: Registry authorities, and the verdict BOTH the Python policy and the shell
protocol must reach for each one. Every entry names the reason, not merely
permitted/refused: two parsers that agree on the verdict while disagreeing
on why have already started to drift.
loopback-address        a supported address form: 127.0.0.0/8, or [::1]
non-loopback-address    a well-formed address that is not loopback
non-loopback-name       a name that is not localhost, however it looks
ipv6-form-not-supported a VALID IPv6 loopback in an unsupported spelling
unbracketed-ipv6        an IPv6 authority without the required brackets
non-numeric-port        a port that is not digits
bracketed-ipv4          brackets are for IPv6 only
$probeLineComment: The line each authority is spliced into for the RECOGNITION check.
It lives here rather than in loopback-corpus.py for a structural reason.
Every filename in boundary.INVENTORY is a token local_script_closure
resolves, so naming a module there puts it in the retention workflow's
script closure, and publication_policy then reads its text as the
workflow's own capability. A control module carrying a literal registry
write verb would therefore fail the pristine tree. Data files are not
scripts and are never walked, so the adversarial vocabulary lives in the
corpus and the module stays free of it -- without widening
boundary.POLICY_SELF, which is the softest part of the design and is not
somewhere to put a new exemption.

entries.name: localhost-bare
entries.why: the supported name form, with no port

entries.name: localhost-port
entries.why: the form the registry controls actually use

entries.name: ipv4-loopback
entries.why: the canonical IPv4 loopback

entries.name: ipv4-loopback-port
entries.why: host and port split on the single colon

entries.name: ipv4-loopback-slash-8
entries.why: the whole of 127.0.0.0/8 is loopback, not just 127.0.0.1

entries.name: ipv6-loopback-bracketed
entries.why: the canonical bracketed IPv6 loopback, which R1 accepted only by string luck

entries.name: ipv6-loopback-bracketed-no-port
entries.why: brackets with no port at all

entries.name: ipv6-loopback-expanded
entries.why: the second supported spelling

entries.name: ipv6-unclosed-bracket
entries.why: malformed; R1 split this on the first colon and compared `[` to a host list

entries.name: ipv6-unbracketed
entries.why: no bracket, so no way to know which colon separates the port

entries.name: ipv6-non-loopback
entries.why: well-formed, bracketed, and somebody else's machine

entries.name: ipv6-remote-global
entries.why: the case R1 could not even MATCH, so it was never classified at all

entries.name: ipv6-unsupported-loopback-spelling
entries.why: a valid IPv6 loopback in a spelling neither side supports; it fails closed

entries.name: ipv6-unsupported-compressed
entries.why: likewise, and refused for that reason rather than mistaken for a remote host

entries.name: ipv6-unspecified
entries.why: the unspecified address is not the loopback address

entries.name: localhost-suffix-trick
entries.why: a name that merely starts with localhost, resolving wherever its owner points it

entries.name: ipv4-suffix-trick
entries.why: five labels is a name, not a dotted quad

entries.name: ipv4-prefix-trick
entries.why: and a loopback quad in the middle of a name is still a name

entries.name: embedded-credentials
entries.why: userinfo is refused even when the host after it is loopback

entries.name: embedded-credentials-remote
entries.why: the credential is the finding; the host does not get a say

entries.name: registry-ghcr
entries.why: the registry this contract must never write to from a validation workflow

entries.name: junk-after-bracket
entries.why: a suffix trick that a bracket-stripping parser would swallow

entries.name: non-numeric-port
entries.why: a port that is not digits is malformed, not a hostname

entries.name: bracketed-ipv4
entries.why: brackets are the IPv6 marker; an IPv4 address inside them is malformed

entries.name: empty-host-port-only
entries.why: a port with nothing in front of it
